$comment: Shared error-taxonomy fixture. All five hosted-login SDKs carry the server error code verbatim on their error type, so a caller in any language can branch on activation_invalid or insufficient_scope. These cases pin the classification every SDK error type must expose, and shape.fallback pins what happens when a response carries no usable code. The code vocabulary is sourced from docs/error-codes.md plus the SDK-originated license and sdk classes: a caller branches on the code, never on the description text.

shape.rule: code is the controlled vocabulary; description is human-facing and may be reworded; neither may be empty for a protocol failure.

fallback.rule: A protocol failure whose body carries no usable error code is reported with this SDK-originated code and the response's own HTTP status. The SDK never substitutes a server code for a response that did not carry one, and never leaves the code empty: an unreadable 500 must not look like a terminal invalid_grant to a caller that branches on the code.

local_validation.rule: A failure the SDK detects before any request keeps code invalid_request with status 0. It is distinguishable from a server code by the zero status. Renaming it would break every existing call site in every language, so the exception is recorded here rather than silently tolerated.

cases.why: Unknown, expired, already claimed, or cross-boundary license and invitation codes all collapse to this one oracle-safe code. An SDK must not add a distinct variant per underlying cause.
The subject has no activation for the requested product; the caller should run setup.
Transient activation-store failure; bounded retry with backoff is the documented response.
Terminal for the grant. Also covers a refresh denied by conditional access, so a caller must not retry refresh indefinitely on this code.
Client authentication failed or was mismatched; opaque on the wire and terminal for the caller.
A requested scope is not registered for the client under the scope registry.
The token is valid but lacks the required scope; distinct from invalid_scope, which means the grant was never issuable.
A DPoP or mTLS sender-constraint failure, or an invalid bearer. Covers every cause indistinguishably.
Unknown WebAuthn session; drives re-ceremony rather than a retry.
Every MFA failure collapses to this code; the SDK must not surface a per-cause variant.
No entitlement projection exists for the tenant; the commercial gate reports absent, never zero.
A subscription mutation was refused because the tenant is already subscribed.
Local entitlement-file verification failed. This code originates in the SDK, not the server, and must never be remapped onto a network error.

invariants: Every protocol failure carries the server error code verbatim; the SDK never invents a local code for a server response.
A response with no usable code is reported as shape.fallback.code, never as a server code and never as an empty string.
Codes originating in the SDK are namespaced by class (license, sdk) and are distinguishable from server codes.
Oracle-safe collapsing is preserved end to end: the SDK exposes one classification per wire code, not per internal cause.
A description is never parsed. Callers branch on code only.
The controlled vocabulary is the union of docs/error-codes.md and the SDK-originated license and sdk classes; adding a case here is a contract change.
